nodes.title: What it cost
nodes.body: Days per client and one to two weeks for a full offering. A missed replace surfaced weeks later as a report a user could not open. No two promotions were identical, so no result could be compared to the last one. The database side was the same: nineteen SQL scripts run one by one in SQL Developer, results copied into spreadsheets.

nodes.title: Days and days of hand edits

slides.title: Now: Every Step Is A Tool With A Test

nodes.title: 1. Export by API
nodes.body: the whole folder in one export task, polled and downloaded

nodes.title: 2. Rewrite by rule
nodes.body: every endpoint, org path and folder replaced by a tested function, longest match first

nodes.title: 3. Carry the datasource
nodes.body: the target's own datasource export goes into the package byte for byte

nodes.title: 4. Verify before import
nodes.body: nothing from the source host survives; every reference exists; every field resolves

nodes.title: 5. Import and read back
nodes.body: re-exported and compared byte for byte; an importer warning is a failure

nodes.title: 6. Execute everything
nodes.body: every view queried, every report rendered, every domain probed for rows

nodes.title: 7. Sign-off generated
nodes.body: PASS, EMPTY or FAIL per resource with timings, one document per org

nodes.title: 8. Same result every time
nodes.body: the same tests, the same order, the same evidence, for every org

nodes.title: Why the result is consistent
nodes.body: The same checks run on every promotion, and the tool stops at the first failure and names the rollback. No person edits a file, so nothing can be missed or typed wrong. Every run leaves its package, its diff and its evidence beside the sign-off, so any two promotions can be compared. Fewer hands in the loop, one outcome.

nodes.title: One command per step, one wrapper for prod
nodes.body: A Python runner takes a step name and a client and runs that step's SQL as the deploy user, logging every statement and result per client. Compound steps chain a stage with its validation so nothing moves on unvalidated. A shell wrapper runs the whole prod sequence, steps 1 to 8, and stops at the first failed gate.

columns.heading: Baseline and validate
items: Creates the eight reporting tables and the views the domains read, then installs the full-history procedures
Submits one database job per table so all eight load in parallel and the session is never the bottleneck
Polls the scheduler's job table until every job is SUCCEEDED; a FAILED or missing job stops the step
Validates row counts per table, twelve monthly totals against the source, and that no grain key repeats
The install gate fails on any empty table or duplicate key, so a wrong grant or filter cannot pass silently

columns.heading: Cutover and validate
items: Installs the rolling procedures: delete the newest months, rebuild them, leave the rest untouched
Runs one operational refresh by hand to prove the rolling path before it is scheduled
Runs the same validation again so the rolling result is compared to the baseline result
Refreshes the domain-support views and checks the aged-balance buckets sum to the balance
Refuses to schedule until both validations are green

columns.heading: Schedule and monitor
items: Creates one scheduler job per table, twice daily, staggered thirty minutes so two never overlap
Long refreshes run as background jobs, never in the session, after a 15-minute timeout once committed a delete without its insert
A capture step records the last run, its duration and its status for every job
High-level data-quality checks run per client and the results are kept with the rollout log
Validate after the baseline, after the cutover, and after the first scheduled run

slides.title: The Objects The Domains Depend On (1 of 2)
rows: CMS_SA_SNAPSHOT
table + refresh procedure

One end-of-day (LDAY) aged-balance row per service agreement: current and payoff balance, new charges, and ten aging buckets built from frozen ARS financial transactions dated up to today. Credits and payments retire the oldest debt first; excess credit sits in the current bucket; buckets 1 to 5 always sum to the current balance; future-dated amounts are excluded.
Debt Management: the SA Snapshot Aged Balance domain, its account roll-up (a derived query over this table, not a second object), and every aged-debt view and dashboard on it
CM_SNAPSHOT_TYPE_FLG
lookup seed
The four snapshot-type codes (LDAY, EMON, ARCH, LEMN) written into the C2M lookup tables. The domain inner-joins them, so a fresh database without the seed returns zero rows in every Ad Hoc view.
Debt Management: SA Snapshot Aged Balance domain
CMS_D1_DVC_IDENTIFIER_VW
view
One row per device with its identifiers pivoted from rows into columns: asset id, badge number, serial number, internal meter number, external and MDM ids, NIC id and serial, name, utility device id.
Meter Operations: Device domain; Daily Installations, Disconnected Service Points, Meters Not Recently Read
CMS_D1_DVC_BODA_VW
view
The device's business-object data area parsed out of its XML: business object code, latest status, retirement date and time. One row per device.
Meter Operations: Device domain
CMS_W1_ASSET_IDENTIFIER_VW
view
One row per asset with its identifiers pivoted into columns, the asset-side twin of the device identifier view, so the Asset domain can join by badge, serial or external id.
Meter Operations: Asset domain; In Storage, Distribution of Installed Assets, Non-Meter Assets

nodes.title: What gets switched on the way
nodes.body: The datasource reference, its alias and the schema's datasource id. The organization path and the destination folder. The tenant root the importer resolves against. Permissions are left to inherit from the folder. When the server version changed, the Ad Hoc topics were repaired by the same path.

nodes.title: Root login on every server; prod writes need an explicit prod flag

columns.heading: What gets rewritten
items: Every absolute repository path from the source org to the target org, longest path first so a folder never clips a file
The destination folder, so a resource can land somewhere other than where it came from
The datasource reference in every report, view and domain, plus the alias and schema id inside the domain XML
The tenant root in the package index so the importer resolves references against the right org
Nothing else: the rewrite is a list of tested replacements, not a free-text edit

columns.heading: What gets verified
items: No string from the source server, source org or source datasource remains anywhere in the package
Every reference a resource makes to something outside the package already exists on the target
Every field an Ad Hoc view uses resolves to an item in its domain, at any nesting depth
The target datasource in the package is byte-identical to the target's own export of it
The org path guard only fires when the two roots differ, so the same org on two servers is allowed

columns.heading: What gets executed
items: Each Ad Hoc view is run through the query engine and must return without error
Each report is rendered to PDF with its default parameters
Each domain is read for its metadata and probed with a query on its root set
The sweep classifies every resource PASS, EMPTY, SLOW or FAIL with its timing
The re-export after import is compared to the package byte for byte, stamps excluded

slides.title: The Automations
rows: Snapshot runner
Runs one deployment step for one client as the deploy user, logging every statement; compound steps pair a stage with its validation
Every step has a log and a gate; nothing moves on unvalidated
Prod rollout wrapper
Runs the whole prod sequence, steps 1 to 8, and stops at the first failed gate
A client is deployed the same way every time
Baseline gate
Polls the database scheduler until every baseline job reports SUCCEEDED
No table is used before its load finished
Install and parity gates
Row counts, monthly totals, duplicate keys, aged-balance buckets against the source
The tables match CISADM before they are scheduled
Repository inventory
Snapshots every resource on an org before a change and diffs after
A rollback record and proof nothing else moved
Promotion
Exports, rewrites, verifies, imports, re-exports, executes any resource from any org to any org
Seven proofs, and prod only with an explicit flag
Domain patch
Applies an additive change to a domain on many orgs, refusing any change that alters what is there
Read-back byte-equal, bound views run, rows tie
Sweep
Executes every view, report and dashboard in a folder and classifies each
PASS, EMPTY, SLOW or FAIL per resource with timing
Sign-off builder
Turns the sweep evidence into the validation document
One document per org, identical structure every time
